svg.title: From contigs to a verified plasmid: what each PlasBench score judges
svg.desc: A five-step schematic. 1 Sequencing contigs. 2 Contig classification and binning. 3 Ordering and orientation. 4 Reconstructed plasmid. 5 Reference validation. Under each step: the score layer that judges it. Three notes: binning is not reconstruction, circular is not correct, and 3D appearance is illustrative.
svg.text: From contigs to a verified plasmid: what each score judges
Schematic, not data. Each step is judged by a different PlasBench score layer; a good score at one step says nothing about the next.

svg.text: Three distinctions this figure keeps explicit

g.text: A tool can put the right contigs in a plasmid's bin without
ordering, orienting or joining them correctly. Bin scores
judge step 2 only; steps 3 to 5 need their own checks.
A circular-looking reconstruction can still hold wrong
joins, missing regions or structural errors. 'Complete
circular' in the scores means the plasmid is covered; it is
not proof the join is right.
The ring is a styled genome map of a sequence, not an
experimentally determined conformation. Any 3D view in this
